summary: Scoped impersonation role for simulated-production inference load testing across projects
description:
Issue summary: Engineering (Perf) needs a narrowly-scoped GCP impersonation role to run simulated-production inference load tests that exercise inter-project networking and Dedicated-like routing behavior.

Impact: Without scoped impersonation, perf team cannot run realistic end-to-end load tests that validate routing/fallback behavior and autoscaling triggers. This delays a performance validation milestone for Dedicated autoscaling improvements.

Request: Provision a service-account impersonation role in project redwood-perf-sim that allows members of project redwood-perf-tools to impersonate a short-lived service account (name: sim-infer-sa@redwood-perf-sim.iam.gserviceaccount.com) with the following constraints: 1) grant iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy and iam.serviceAccounts.get on the target SA, 2) allow iam.serviceAccounts.actAs for the impersonating identity, 3) binding limited to the group perf-testing@redwood.com, 4) TTL-limited credentials (max 6 hours).

Background/context: The scheduled load tests mimic production traffic patterns (streaming + prefix caching + multi-model routing) across two projects to validate cross-project fallback routing and autoscaler signal fidelity. Previous ad-hoc long-lived credentials caused audit noise and elevated scope. Security asked for scoped impersonation instead of broad role assignments.

Proposed role and bindings (draft):
- Custom role: roles/perfSimImpersonator (permissions: iam.serviceAccounts.get, iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy, iam.serviceAccounts.actAs)
- Binding: principals: group:perf-testing@redwood.com -> role: roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (on sim-infer-sa only) and custom role at project level to allow listing/checking.
- Conditions: resource.name match to the sim-infer-sa service account and binding expiry 2026-03-14 18:00 UTC unless extended with justification.

Audit & safety: All impersonation activity must be logged to BigQuery audit dataset perf_audit and alerts should be configured if impersonation token lifetime > 6h or if requests originate from unexpected IP ranges.

Deliverables expected: 1) IAM policy patch committed and applied, 2) short walkthrough for perf team on how to acquire impersonation tokens, 3) verification steps in CI that confirm impersonation tokens are scoped and expire, 4) Confluence runbook link added to related_confluence_pages.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Attempt to run perf tooling from project redwood-perf-tools that creates an inference job in redwood-perf-sim using current SA credentials.
2) Observe 403s or failures related to iam.serviceAccounts.actAs when tools attempt to launch inference tasks under sim-infer-sa.
3) Confirm impersonation not allowed by calling `gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy sim-infer-sa@redwood-perf-sim.iam.gserviceaccount.com` from perf-tools project and noting missing bindings.
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed via Cloud Audit Logs that previous perf jobs used long-lived credentials originating from developer laptops (entries in audit log 2026-03-05).
- SRE verified that the target SA exists and is active (sim-infer-sa).
- Perf tooling currently expects to call generateAccessToken for impersonation; current bindings only allow it for project owners causing manual intervention.
- Security rep (Marco Liu) requested minimal privileges and TTL enforcement; suggested using IAM Conditions and short-lived tokens.
- Risk: if misconfigured, impersonation tokens could be used to spin up heavy GPU-backed jobs; recommended restricting to specific compute instance templates and preflight quotas.
